A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Learning in Structured Stackelberg Games. Their complete main text, figures, payoff tables, algorithms and Appendices A–D support comparison despite reformatting, renumbering and relocated content.

before.justification: v3 reports algorithms, theoretical bounds, proofs and constructed game examples, including in its appendices, but no original experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v4 retains the theoretical results and constructions. Its additional application citations and future directions do not report original empirical outcomes; none appear in the appendices.

M1.justification: SSOA, the Stackelberg Distributional Learner and the multiclass decision-list algorithm retain the same procedures (Algorithms 1–3). Relocating the computational discussion and explaining possible context representations do not change the methods.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or application tasks. v4's added natural-language context and inference-time alignment examples are motivation; the theoretical auction and persuasion applications in Appendix A are retained.

E2.justification: The same SOA comparison and counterexample remain in Section 3.3 and Appendix B. Newly cited studies do not introduce evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an empirical evaluation protocol. The adversarial online setting with follower-type feedback and the i.i.d. distributional learning setting are unchanged.

E4.justification: The illustrative game and tree constructions, including the Appendix B SOA analysis, are retained. Neither version reports ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness experiments or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeats, seeds, error bars or significance tests. The theoretical PAC confidence parameters and concentration arguments remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their payoff values, and the worked results match, including optimal regret 3/4 versus SOA regret 2 in Appendix B. No empirical result entries are added.

T1.justification: The SL/SN/SG definitions, regret bounds, PAC guarantees and appendix proofs are substantively unchanged. v3's decision-list Theorem D.2 becomes v4's Theorem 5.1 with the same O(nKL) mistake bound. Notation explanations and typesetting corrections do not alter the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: structured Stackelberg learning, an instance-optimal SL characterization and algorithm, and distributional sample-complexity bounds. The computational result promoted into the main text already appeared in v3.

C2.justification: v4 Section 6 expands v3's computational and agnostic-learning discussion with a possible efficiency–optimality tradeoff, smoothed beyond-worst-case analysis, and extensions to multiple followers and bandit feedback. These additions clarify specific open questions and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode and Appendix B.1's finite-strategy approximation details are unchanged. Neither version supplies implementation hyperparameters, hardware specifications, measured runtimes or code/data access information.

R1.justification: v4 adds references on reward shaping, meta-learning, smoothed analysis and multi-follower games: Wang et al. (2026a), Harris et al. (2023), Block et al. (2022), Haghtalab et al. (2024), and Personnat et al. (2025). It also removes v3's broad statement that computational considerations were largely ignored, modestly refining the positioning.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. The computational overview, decision-list example and theorem move from Appendix D to Section 5, while the proof remains in Appendix D. v4 expands and organizes the conclusion, edits motivation and acknowledgments, adds an Impact Statement, and changes citation style.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column conference layout, with running headers and reflowed equations and algorithms. Existing figures are resized or relocated, Table 1 becomes a 2-by-2 panel arrangement, and Figure 1's caption explains its notation. The underlying figure images are identical.

improvement.justification: Moving the computational overview from Appendix D into Section 5, explaining Figure 1's notation, and expanding Section 6's specific open questions improve accessibility and framing. The algorithms, proofs and supporting examples remain substantively unchanged, so the evidence supports a limited overall quality gain.
